items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was married to Jerry [Jerome] Kern’s daughter, Betty.

ctx.x: When you came back, what did you do?

Oh, boy. That was a low spot. I was married to Jerry [Jerome] Kern’s daughter, Betty. And I had a kid, Steve. My first kid. It was . . . The marriage was no good. It was hopeless. And I knew it, but I tried to stay with it as long as I could. It didn’t work. Finally there was nothing to do. Got divorced, which is a miserable experience. Whatever you want to say about it, any marriage, a divorce is a miserable experience. So that was a low spot, and I got into psychoanalysis, which began a slow ascent back to…

1100 dollars. So, multiply by 10 if you want, or 15. In any case, the analysis began to take root, but I was a totally confused person, about music, about me. What was I doing? Music obviously was part of it. But I didn’t want to play. I didn’t do any more of that. I was disillusioned.
